english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function such that the function $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $g(x)=(x+1)f(x)$ is an odd function, and
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक सतत फलन है, इस प्रकार कि $g(x)=(x+1)f(x)$ द्वारा परिभाषित फलन $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक विषम फलन है, तथा सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए
solution: Write $f=E+O$ ($E$ even, $O$ odd). Then $(x+1)f=\big(xE+O\big)+\big(xO+E\big)$, where $xE+O$ is odd and $xO+E$ is even
$g$ odd $\Rightarrow$ its even part is zero: $E(x)=-xO(x)$
solution_full: Every $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is uniquely $f=E+O$ with $E(x)=\dfrac{f(x)+f(-x)}{2}$ even and $O(x)=\dfrac{f(x)-f(-x)}{2}$ odd; both are continuous because $f$ is.

$g(x)=(x+1)f(x)=xE(x)+xO(x)+E(x)+O(x)$. The product of the odd function $x$ with an even function is odd and with an odd function is even. So the odd part of $g$ is $xE(x)+O(x)$ and the even part of $g$ is $xO(x)+E(x)$.
$g$ is odd, so its even part vanishes: $E(x)=-xO(x)$ for all $x$.

For an odd continuous function $\displaystyle\int_{-x}^{x}O(t)\,dt=0$, and for an even one $\displaystyle\int_{-x}^{x}E(t)\,dt=2\int_{0}^{x}E(t)\,dt$. Hence $2\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}E(t)\,dt=-\dfrac{2x^{5}}{5}$ for all $x$; differentiating, $2E(x)=-2x^{4}$, so $E(x)=-x^{4}$.
Then $-xO(x)=-x^{4}$ gives $O(x)=x^{3}$ for $x\ne0$, and $O(0)=0$ for any odd function, so $O(x)=x^{3}$ for all $x$.
originality_note: New: f is recovered from two parity conditions - the product (x+1)f(x) is odd, which ties the even part to the odd part (E = -xO), and a symmetric integral that sees only the even part (way 5). Closest known: f(x) + f(-x) = c type questions (ax^5 + b sin x + c) and simple even/odd decomposition. Different because: neither part of f is given directly; the parity of a product and the vanishing of the integral of an odd function must both be used.

key_step: Splitting (x+1)f(x) into odd part xE + O and even part xO + E, so E = -xO, then using that the symmetric integral sees only E.
justification: Two parity properties must be combined (parity of a product, integral of odd/even functions over [-x, x]) to recover f; neither alone suffices, numerical answer. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q7 (L3), which reasons about g = x f(x) and parity/regularity implications.

concept_use.Even and odd functions; decomposition in: f is split as E + O, and the odd part of (x+1)f(x) is xE + O while its even part is xO + E, so g odd forces E = -xO.
concept_use.Property for odd and even functions: Properties of odd and even functions: x times an even function is odd, x times an odd function is even, the integral of an odd function over [-x, x] is 0, and that of an even function is twice the integral over [0, x].
